    +4positive 4

    • Projected Line:
      +4positive 4

    • Cut History: The cut line usually falls between 2-over and 6-over, with a 4-over cut being common (2023, 2021, 2019). 
    Note: The cut line is fluid and can change during the second round, but

    What is the cut for the Masters 2026?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    For the 2026 Masters Tournament, the cut rule is the top 50 players and ties after 36 holes, with the 10-shot rule no longer in effect. After two rounds, only those 50 and ties advance to play the weekend rounds, a rule in place since 2020. The field is typically reduced from around 91 players, making the cutline very tight. 
    Key Details for the 2026 Masters Cut: 
    • Threshold: Only the top 50 scores and ties advance.
    • No 10-Shot Rule: Players within 10 strokes of the leader who are outside the top 50 do not make the cut, unlike in years past.
    • Timing: The cut is made at the end of Friday's second round.
    • 2026 Outlook: With roughly 91 players in the field and conditions potentially favoring lower scores, a tough cut line around 4-over 148 is expected. 
    Synonyms and Terms for "Cut": 
    • Made the Weekend: Advancing to play rounds 3 and 4.
    • Top 50 and Ties: The specific requirement for the 2026 tournament.
    • Field Reduction: The process of eliminating players.
    • Surviving the Cut: Players who make the cutline. 
    Players who miss the cut, which in 2026 included various high-profile names, do not compete on Saturday or Sunday.
